## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Loka Sutta* ("The World", Iti 112; It 4.13, PTS It 121) is a discourse in the *Catukkanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text sets forth the worldly dimensions comprehended by the Buddha and the distinctive spiritual attainments that entitle him to be known as the Tathāgata [SuttaCentral]. It culminates in verses celebrating the Tathāgata as the tamed, peaceful, and liberated sage who liberates others [Levman 2014]. In a study of Buddhist verse style and Middle Indo-Aryan phonetics, Bryan Geoffrey Levman analyzes these lines (*danto damayataṁ seṭṭho santo samayataṁ isi / mutto mocayataṁ aggo tiṇṇo tārayataṁ varo*), noting the composer's deliberate use of sonorous parallel structures and causative participial forms [Levman 2014]. In doctrinal studies, the sutta is cited as an early canonical authority affirming that the Tathāgata truly speaks and expounds the Dhamma, a passage highlighted by Louis de La Vallée Poussin to contrast early Buddhist understandings of the Buddha with Madhyamaka perspectives [Tillemans 1992].
The text has a verbatim parallel in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4.23, also titled *Lokasutta*), sharing nearly its entirety (§2.1–13.4 ↔ §23.0.3–23.12.4) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus both confirm a full Chinese parallel in the *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 137, 世間; T 26.29) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further records over two hundred Pali-internal reuse passages across thirty texts, showing shared segments with the *Pāsādika Sutta* (DN 29, §3.1–6.2) and the *Posālamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 18), as well as extensive treatment in the commentaries to the *Itivuttaka*, *Mahāniddesa*, *Udāna*, and *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [DharmaNexus]. Automated alignments also register textual correspondences in Tibetan canonical literature, including the *Kuśalamūlaparidhara-sūtra* (D 101) and the *Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra* (D 301) [DharmaNexus].
